findings.detail: The Background & Objectives section adds an unnecessary historic valuation despite the brief to keep it high level. More importantly, Recommendations does not give the known approximate inheritance amount or explain why the proposed transactions are suitable, as the specification requires.
report_quote: Your joint General Investment Account was previously shown in our records (10 March) as £30,000.
We recommend using the inheritance together with the proceeds to fund both Robert's and Jean's ISAs for the new tax year.

findings.detail: The meeting note says Jean would find the cash-account paperwork and its details would be confirmed before anything was finalised; the report reduces this to a passing mention. It also presents the approximately £38,000 seen on screen at the meeting as prospective sale proceeds, which may differ when the disposal takes place.
report_quote: Jean also mentioned a separate cash account from some years ago, although she was unsure whether it remains active.
We recommend using the gross proceeds of c. £38,000 to fund both ISAs and the new jointly-held investment account.

findings.detail: The report mentions an inheritance but silently omits the requested sensitive acknowledgement that it followed the recent death of Jean's mother. It does not leak the internal guidance.
report_quote: We recommend using the inheritance together with the proceeds to fund both Robert's and Jean's ISAs for the new tax year.

findings.detail: The report shifts between speaking about the clients and addressing them, uses the technical word ‘disinvest’, and does not explain what the initial charge applies to. These make an otherwise readable report less clear.
report_quote: The couple’s objectives remain unchanged: they wish to invest alongside their existing portfolio for long-term growth, with no income required for the foreseeable future.
We recommend that you disinvest the joint GIA.
The initial charge that applies is 0.5%.

findings.detail: The missing amounts are identifiable, but this marker would be more actionable if it named Robert’s and Jean’s respective ISAs and their proposed joint account, rather than relying on the surrounding text to identify them.
report_quote: [ADVISER TO CONFIRM #5: ISA top-up amounts and the resulting balance for the new account]
